text: La brecha entre KOSPI y Taiwán se ha vuelto extrema. Corea es esencialmente una apuesta apalancada en el ciclo de la memoria, mientras que Taiwán está dominado por TSMC y el ecosistema de fabricación de semiconductores avanzados. El mercado cuestiona cada vez más la sostenibilidad de los beneficios derivados de la memoria, al tiempo que sigue premiando la historia de la infraestructura estructural de IA. La cuestión más importante es si Corea simplemente está experimentando un reajuste de ganancias específico del sector de la memoria, o si es el primer mercado en reconocer que la economía del auge de la IA se está volviendo más compleja.

China Onshore Tech YTD gains wiped out China's ChiNext index (US: $CNXT) now sitting on the 150-week EMA.. sell-off in onshore China tech has been breathtaking (+39% ytd in June to now -9%) despite exports roofing Star50 has been destroyed too, nearing its 150W EMA (US: $KSTR). Was +71% ytd in June, now +5% Why this nonstop selling? - concerns that an FCC rule (https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/us-fcc-vote-ban-chinese-labs-testing-us-electronics-2026-10-07/), or broader import limits on Chinese products - MATCH Act would put pressure on the A-share AI domestic supply chain The counter is.. - there's no quick or easy replacement for China.. $LITE CEO "optical components are completely sold out" through early 2029, & disruption to the supply chain would be taken as a negative, as Chinese players take ~70% of US transceiver market share - China has leverage on indium phosphide, which relies on indium mostly from China, now under export control (https://www.mofcom.gov.cn/cms_files/filemanager/policySummary/viewcore_eecb876dd3e440deaab226390c863807.html) Looks like the trade war is intensifying behind the scenes. Might also be why US AI CapEx players are getting creamed since they rely heavily on China onshore players which isn't talked about enough. Potential Trump/Xi meeting in Nov for APEC in Shenzhen and Dec for G20 in Miami might be near-term relief points
